authorisation: Product-Owner instruction to continue the EXISTING functional-completeness closure mission for final repository/governance closure only. Explicitly repository-only: no PRE-LIVE contact or change, no deployment, restart, migration, networking change, Guest activation, PMS/financial/provider traffic and no Go-Live. No new mission was started and no new environment authorisation was taken.
what_this_closes:
The technical acceptance finished at T0180, but the authoritative state was not closure-consistent. It simultaneously declared every gap closed and went on presenting the closure as the CURRENT WORK while retaining an executable authorisation to act on PRE-LIVE 172.21.60.25. That is not cosmetic: next_authorized_action, blockers and allowed_actions are the fields an agent reads before touching a live appliance, and a spent authorisation left in them is indistinguishable from a live one.

FIVE CONTRADICTIONS WERE PRESENT ON MASTER, and each is now retired:
  1. next_authorized_action -- 'Execute to DONE the ... FUNCTIONAL-COMPLETENESS CLOSURE ... including the controlled PRE-LIVE work on 172.21.60.25 the mission names'.
  2. blockers[0] -- 'THE CURRENT WORK IS THE FUNCTIONAL-COMPLETENESS CLOSURE ... What remains is execution'.
  3. allowed_actions[0] -- 'Execute the authorised functional-completeness closure to DONE ... including controlled work on PRE-LIVE 172.21.60.25'.
  4. authorized_activities -- the post-roadmap DEVELOPMENT appliance trial still AUTHORIZED_IN_PROGRESS since D29/T0066, against 172.21.60.23, which this same file records as RETIRED and forbidden to contact. An authorisation whose target may not be touched is not in progress.
  5. functional_completeness_remaining.increment_3.known_gap_not_closed -- a key whose NAME asserted an unclosed required gap, beside a _state declaring every gap closed.

THIS IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF THE CONTRADICTION INCREMENT 2 FIXED. There the register FORBADE what the Product Owner had authorised; here it went on AUTHORISING what had already finished. The same file, the same fields, the opposite direction -- which is why the fix is a validator rather than an edit.
the_increment_3_gap_was_re_determined_no:
The Product Owner asked for this to be settled from current evidence and not papered over. It was, repository-only, against a disposable PostgreSQL.

THE CLAIM: 'scripts/pmsd-pg-integration.sh applies a curated migration list ending at 0079, so 0080-0087 have no gate-enforced integration coverage.'

THE FIRST CLAUSE IS STILL TRUE. That list still ends at 0079_recovery_belongs_to_the_connection_not_the_building, and the repository is now at 0090.

THE CONCLUSION IS FALSE. Those migrations are covered by the SAME required gate, from a different step. phase3-full-software-gate step 'factory-clean-baseline' runs scripts/clean-install-reconstruction.sh, which applies migrations by GLOB -- `ls $MIG/*.up.sql | sort` -- from a BLANK cluster with no curated list, then asserts LEDGER COMPLETENESS: every migration and every iam_base step must appear in public.schema_migrations or the step fails. The same step runs factory-clean-baseline-verify.sh, which compares that end state against the upgrade path's catalog fact by fact. Independently, the governance gate runs tools/validate-migration-grant-durability.py, which also globs every migration -- and that is the check which caught the four REAL defects in this very range: 0080, 0081, 0082 and 0083 each added an operator read Gate-P did not mirror, so a rebuilt appliance would have lost all four.

RE-VERIFIED FOR THIS RECLASSIFICATION (2026-09-23): CLEAN_INSTALL_RECONSTRUCTION = PASS. 0080 through 0090 each applied `ok` in chain order. 'every migration and base step is represented in the ledger'. 96 iam_v2 tables, 9,960 catalog facts, identity-bearing tables empty. No PRE-LIVE contact.

CLASSIFIED PRECISELY, NOT GENEROUSLY. Post-0079 migrations have STRUCTURAL and PRIVILEGE coverage -- they apply in order from factory-clean, they are recorded, both install paths agree, their grants survive a Gate-P reconcile -- but NOT BEHAVIOURAL suite coverage: pmsd-pg-integration.sh's eleven Phase-3 suites stop at 0079 and phase5-pg-integration.sh's chain stops at 0080. This is a limitation of two suites' scope, and it is NOT equivalence -- it is weaker in a named, bounded way. It is recorded as increment_3.migration_suite_scope_limitation, a DOCUMENTED NON-BLOCKING LIMITATION, and the superseded text is preserved verbatim in _reclassification_audit so the change is auditable rather than a deletion.

WHY NON-BLOCKING. The failure mode a curated list creates is a migration that never runs in CI, and the glob path closes it on every delivery. The failure mode that actually occurred here -- a privilege existing only in a migration -- is closed by a validator that also globs. The product behaviour those migrations back was verified live across increments 3, 4 and 5. What is missing is a second, behavioural proof of already-proven behaviour.

THE CURATED LIST IS STILL NOT EXTENDED, for the reason first recorded: extending it means tracing each migration's dependencies through a hand-maintained file whose breakage breaks the phase3 gate for every delivery. Instead the coverage the classification DEPENDS on is now itself gate-protected (see below).
the_validator_is_the_actual_deliverable:
An edit fixes this once. A rule stops it recurring, and the Product Owner asked for the rule.

tools/project-state.py gains check_closure_coherence, wired into `validate` beside the existing state-contradiction hook, so it runs in the governance gate AND in the adversarial mutation suite -- the one thing that proves a rule can fail. It is CONDITIONAL on the state declaring closure, because before that an execution authorisation is correct and an open gap is honest; a rule that fired then would demand the register lie about work in flight. Closure is declared by two new machine-readable fields, functional_completeness_verdict = PASS and functional_completeness_mission_status = CLOSED, so the declaration and the restrictions it implies cannot drift apart.

Once closure is declared it refuses: an execution authorisation in next_authorized_action, blockers or allowed_actions (matched on an execution verb plus a closure/PRE-LIVE object, with past-tense reporting excused so the record may still DESCRIBE what happened); any authorized_activities entry left AUTHORIZED_IN_PROGRESS; any key under functional_completeness_remaining whose NAME says a required gap is not closed; and any gap-register entry that does not open by stating it is closed or a documented non-blocking limitation.

A FIRST VERSION OF THE RULE WAS TOO NARROW AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH. Matching the verb 'execute' caught four of the five contradictions and let blockers[0] through, because that sentence read 'What remains is EXECUTION'. The match is now on 'execut' plus the phrasings that present something as the current work. That is exactly the failure a rule like this exists to prevent, so it is written down rather than quietly widened.

AND THE JUSTIFICATION IS CHECKED, NOT TRUSTED. The non-blocking classification above leans entirely on the reconstruction applying migrations by glob and asserting ledger completeness. A companion check refuses a clean-install-reconstruction.sh that has lost either one -- so converting that script to a curated list turns the documented limitation back into a real gap AND fails the gate that accepted the classification.

PROVEN BOTH WAYS. Declaring closure on master's unreconciled state produced exactly five FAILs, one per contradiction. Six new adversarial mutations (M66-M71) reintroduce each contradiction and the loss of the glob, and the suite requires every one to be detected.
what_this_delivery_did_not_do: No PRE-LIVE contact of any kind: no deployment, no service restart, no migration, no networking or DHCP change, no schema or data change, no capability enablement, no Guest activation, no PMS or payment-provider traffic, no Go-Live. The disposable PostgreSQL used for the reclassification evidence was a local container built from repository sources and destroyed afterwards. No product behaviour changed -- the only non-governance files touched are a validator and its test suite.

closure_verdict.product_owner_decisions_not_gaps: HA architecture, payment-provider selection, the C35 external archival receipt authority, and the master approving-review policy. These are DECISIONS, not technical gaps, not blockers on this mission, and closing them is not engineering work.

the_keyword_validator_had_no_word_for_a_:
The adversarial mutation suite refuses to run until the GOOD state passes both validators, and it refused: BASELINE FAIL structural=0 keyword=1. The governance gate failed the same way on the same step, so this was caught by the mechanism built for it rather than by reading.

THE CAUSE WAS A WHITELIST WITH NO ENTRY FOR THIS STATE. validate-project-state.sh extracts `next authorized (activity|action|step)[^.]*` from both pack files and requires the result to match one of a long list of legitimate phrasings -- every phase added its own as it arrived. There was an entry for 'Execute to DONE the Product-Owner-authorised FUNCTIONAL-COMPLETENESS CLOSURE' and none for that mission being finished.

AND THE EXTRACTOR STOPS AT THE FIRST PERIOD, which made the first attempt unfixable by adding a pattern: the field opened 'NONE. The Product-Owner ...', so the candidate string was the single word 'NONE' and no phrase could be matched against it. The field now states its claim BEFORE the first period, and the allow-list gains the CLOSED phrasing. That is an addition -- it recognises a new legitimate state and removes no check.
review_found_two_holes_in_the_rule_itsel:
Three findings on PR #179, all genuine, and two of them defects in the very rule this delivery exists to add. Recorded because a validator that fails open is worse than no validator: it reports PASS.

P1, THE SAFEGUARD COULD BE SWITCHED OFF BY DELETING TWO KEYS. The closure rules were conditional on functional_completeness_mission_status and functional_completeness_verdict, and nothing else in the repository required either one. Delete both and `declared` goes false, every rule below silently stops running, and the state still reports PROJECT_STATE_GOVERNANCE = PASS. The condition is now anchored to the MISSION CLOSURE RECEIPT: a transition recording FUNCTIONAL_COMPLETENESS_MISSION_CLOSURE is a permanent historical fact, so once one exists the sentinels must exist and must read closed. Deleting them fails, and the rules are evaluated anyway so the deletion buys no free pass on a retained authorisation.

P2, THE BAN WAS TOO BROAD AND WOULD HAVE BEEN FELT LATER. It refused EVERY in-progress activity, so with the closure permanently recorded any future Product-Owner-authorised work, under a new decision and unrelated to this mission, would have failed validation simply for existing -- a register unable to state what is authorised, which is the defect this file exists to prevent, reintroduced by the fix for its mirror image. The ban is now scoped to the two kinds of entry it is about: one tied to the mission that just closed, and one whose target is an appliance this same state records as RETIRED. The retired addresses are read from prohibited_actions rather than hardcoded.

P1, THE HEADING IS NOT THE CHECK. The ledger guard matched the words 'ledger completeness', which live in an echo banner, so the loop underneath could be deleted while the heading, the match and the PASS all survived. apply_one swallows the ledger INSERT with `|| true`, so a migration really can apply without being recorded and that loop is the only thing that notices. The executable assertion is now required: the per-migration schema_migrations query AND the failure it raises.

PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because the mutation suite proves a rule can FAIL and cannot prove a rule stays QUIET when it should -- which is how two of these three would have shipped. New mutations M72 (sentinels removed) and M73 (ledger loop deleted, heading kept), and a new committed runner, tools/tests/closure_coherence/run_negative.py, with 15 assertions wired into the governance gate: each contradiction is refused, AND a new activity under a new decision, a next action for unrelated authorised work, and blockers merely DESCRIBING the completed closure are all allowed. It gutters the reconstruction script to prove the ledger check, then restores it byte-exact and verifies that it did.
an_unclassified_gate_step_is_refused_and:
Adding the closure-coherence step to project-governance.yml without classifying it in governance/ci-reuse-policy.json failed the governance gate at CI_REUSE_POLICY: 'a step nobody has classified must not inherit a reuse guard by accident'. That is a control I had not met, doing exactly what it exists for -- a new step carrying `if: steps.reuse.outputs.hit != 'true'` would otherwise have been skipped on an evidence-reuse hit with nobody having decided that was safe.

Classified tree-pure, like every sibling negative-test step: the runner builds in-process variations of the tracked project-state.json and runs the tracked rule against them, and its one filesystem case restores clean-install-reconstruction.sh byte-exact and verifies that it did. Every input is the tree, so an identical tree gives an identical verdict.
